title: Ankhorage Contracts
summary: Defines portable, serializable contracts exchanged by independent application, tooling, runtime, and adapter packages.
purpose: Provide stable runtime-neutral data boundaries so separately released packages can exchange manifests, descriptors, plans, and configuration without sharing implementation code.
responsibilities: Own cross-repository serializable declarations for application manifests, capabilities, bindings, data, deployment, infrastructure, media, navigation, rules, secrets, state, storage, UI, websites, and flows.
Publish contract topics through explicit package subpaths for independent consumers.
Provide deterministic parsers and structural validators for the portable document shapes that require runtime decoding.
boundaries: Does not execute application capabilities, deployment plans, infrastructure operations, navigation, storage, authentication, or other provider behavior.
Does not own framework-specific or provider-specific adapters and composition.
Does not maintain reverse consumer inventories or application-specific business workflows.
audience: Authors of independently released packages that exchange Ankhorage documents and descriptors.
Tooling and runtime maintainers that decode or validate portable Ankhorage data.
useCases: Define a portable application manifest and its screen, theme, binding, data, media, and navigation values.
Exchange capability, infrastructure, deployment, repository, rules, and flow descriptors across package boundaries.
Decode supported serialized documents without importing an implementation-owning repository.

architecture.role: Central package for shared portable declarations and deterministic structural decoding at public topic subpaths.
invariants: Cross-repository contracts remain serializable and reconstructable without repository-local runtime objects.
Consumers use published package subpaths and declared dependencies rather than sibling source imports.
Provider selection, side effects, and framework-specific implementation remain outside this package.

limitations: A declaration belongs here only when at least two repositories require the same portable contract.
Structural decoders validate only the document shapes explicitly owned by this package.
